section_summary: This section documents U.S. State Department and SCAP monitoring of Japanese corporate combines (zaibatsu), private trade restrictions, and foreign property interests following World War II. It features a detailed wartime German intelligence report analyzing the structure and operations of the major Japanese Konzerne, alongside SCAP directives enforcing asset freezes and penal sanctions on designated restricted concerns. The correspondence also traces inquiries from American businesses, including Sims & Company regarding private import-export operations, Paramount Films regarding the restitution of pre-war securities holdings, and Toyo Menka Kaisha regarding corporate reorganization.

subfiles.about: Intelligence study translating a German analysis of the organizational structure, holdings, and wartime role of major Japanese industrial combines.
subfiles.from: Captured Personnel and Material Branch, Military Intelligence Division, War Department
subfiles.summary: This report translates a study by the German East Asia Society detailing the history, capital structure, and wartime cartelization of Japanese industrial combines. It surveys the major combines including Mitsui, Mitsubishi, Sumitomo, and Nissan, outlining their subsidiaries, bank deposits, and heavy industry conversions under Japan's planned war economy. Secondary combines such as Okura, Yasuda, Nichitsu, Furukawa, Asano, Nomura, Showa, Riken, and Kobe Seiko are also cataloged.
subfiles.title: Report No. 1599: Japanese Konzerne
